sections.title: Event Overview
sections.body: PERMIRA Summer Camp 2026 (PERMIRA Camp 3.0 — III Indonesian–Russian Students Summer Camp) is a three-day youth diplomacy and cultural-exchange programme organised by PERMIRA St. Petersburg, the Indonesian Students' Association in Russia. It is held as part of the celebration of 76 years of Indonesia–Russia diplomatic relations and the Saint Petersburg Year of Culture. Theme: "Taste of Nusantara: The Eco-Culinary Bridge from ASEAN to Russia". Dates: 19–21 July 2026. Location: Kubenskiy Island — a boreal island in the Kivi Park regional nature reserve, Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast (Lake Vuoksa / Gulf of Finland). It is reached only by boat and, being a conservation area, has no power grid or phone signal — pure focus on cooking, nature, and each other.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: The camp strengthens youth diplomacy between Indonesia and Russia, with ASEAN participation, focused on cultural, language, and historical exchange among students. It uses cuisine as an inclusive medium for cross-cultural collaboration, alongside an environmental-stewardship ethic (waste sorting, reduced single-use plastic, efficient food portions). It is a friendship and cultural programme — not an environmental conference.

sections.title: Participants
sections.body: Capacity is 35 students: 15 from Indonesia, 10 from Russia, and 10 from ASEAN countries. Participants are active university students in Russia (aged 18 or over, no upper limit), verified by a Russian university student card (Studencheskiy Bilet / Propusk), with basic conversational English. Indonesian participants must also be registered in the PERMIRA St. Petersburg database and have completed Indonesian citizen self-reporting (lapor diri).

sections.title: Getting there & meeting point
sections.body: On Day 1 (19 July), participants gather at Ozerki metro station in Saint Petersburg at 09:00 MSK, where volunteers will meet the group. Transfer to the camp runs 10:00–13:00 MSK: first by bus to the village of Chulkovo in Leningrad Oblast (10:00–12:30), then by speedboat across to Kubenskiy Island in the Kivi Park nature reserve, Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast (12:30–13:00). Please arrive on time — the group travels together and latecomers cannot be accommodated. On arrival, each participant is shown to a tent labelled with their name in Russian and Indonesian, followed by a safety briefing in Russian with Indonesian and English translation.

sections.title: Programme
sections.body:
Day 1 (19 July) — Arrive & Settle: 09:00 gather at Ozerki metro; 10:00–13:00 transfer by bus (to Chulkovo) and speedboat (to the island); 13:00 tent placement and safety briefing; 14:00 tent setup & group photo; 15:30 ice-breaking & team bonding; 16:30 fun team games; 18:00 dinner; 19:00 fun session (sharing & storytelling); 22:00 rest. (All times MSK.)
Day 2 (20 July) — Cook & Connect: morning activity & light reflection; breakfast; Culinary Masterclass & Cooking Session (Sate Madura, Ayam Lengkuas, Soto Ayam); lunch from what you cooked; cooking challenge & presentation; free time & documentation; dinner; fun night & games; a Capture-the-Moment screening & closing circle; and an optional late-night campfire.
Day 3 (21 July) — Reflect & Farewell: breakfast and prep to leave; tent break-down; last documentation & farewell; awarding & appreciation (best cooking, team collaboration, team spirit, most active, best capture); and the final closing session.
A separate bilingual opening/welcome with guest remarks may accompany Day 1 — see the Opening ceremony section.

sections.title: Opening ceremony
sections.body: The official opening runs 13:30–14:35 MSK on 19 July, hosted bilingually by Indonesian and Russian presenters and broadcast live at summercamp2026.permiraspb.org. Programme: the national anthems of Indonesia and Russia; remarks from H.E. José Antonio Morató Tavares (Ambassador of the Republic of Indonesia to the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus), Honorary Consul Valery Radchenko, and Leningrad Oblast officials (the Committee on Natural Resources, the Committee on External Relations, the Directorate of Specially Protected Natural Areas, and the Leningrad branch of the All-Russian Society for Nature Conservation), together with the chairs of the PERMIRA Central Committee and PERMIRA St. Petersburg; and the cutting of a traditional tumpeng followed by a group photo.

sections.title: Cuisine
sections.body: Cooking is the central shared activity. In the Culinary Masterclass & Cooking Sessions, mixed teams of Indonesian, Russian, and ASEAN students cook Indonesian dishes together and learn the ingredients, techniques, and cultural stories behind them. Example dishes that illustrate Indonesian culinary heritage include Sate Madura, Ayam Lengkuas, and Soto Ayam. Actual dishes may vary depending on programme arrangements and availability.

sections.title: Meals
sections.body: All meals are provided during the camp. On Day 1, lunch is rice, egg with tomato, and chicken sausages; dinner is grilled chicken with rice and a vegetable mix. Menus may vary. In line with the camp's environmental ethic, participants are asked to bring their own reusable cutlery and drink container and to take efficient portions to reduce food waste.

sections.title: Environmental Stewardship
sections.body: As a commitment to sustainability, participants are asked to: bring their own reusable cutlery and drink containers; take efficient food portions to reduce food waste; sort waste into three categories (organic, non-organic, and hazardous/B3 such as glass, ink, medicine, or batteries); and minimise paper and single-use plastic — including using QR codes instead of paper during games and registration.

sections.title: Registration
sections.body: Reserve a place through the website's registration form. Requirements: a valid passport; a Russian university student card (Studencheskiy Bilet / Propusk); minimum age 18 (no upper limit); status as an active university student in Russia; basic conversational English; and genuine interest in culture and cuisine with willingness to participate fully, including cooking and team activities. You upload both the passport and student card in the form. Indonesian applicants must be registered in the PERMIRA St. Petersburg database and have completed lapor diri (peduliwni.kemlu.go.id). Priority is given to Indonesian students in a Russian-language preparatory class. Selected participants are notified by email.

sections.title: Languages
sections.body: The programme is conducted in Indonesian and Russian. Basic conversational English is required of all participants to support cross-cultural interaction.

faqs.question: Where and when do we meet?
faqs.answer: On 19 July, gather at Ozerki metro station in Saint Petersburg at 09:00 MSK. Volunteers will meet you there, then the group transfers together by bus to Chulkovo and by boat to Kubenskiy Island. Please be on time — the group leaves together.

faqs.question: Where is the camp?
faqs.answer: On Kubenskiy Island in the Kivi Park regional nature reserve, Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast. The island is off-grid (no electricity or phone signal) and reached by boat from the village of Chulkovo.

faqs.question: Can I watch the opening ceremony online?
faqs.answer: Yes. The opening ceremony on 19 July (13:30–14:35 MSK) is streamed live at summercamp2026.permiraspb.org.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: Programme participation, meals, and accommodation during the camp are provided for selected participants. Details are confirmed during selection.

faqs.question: Who can join?
faqs.answer: Active university students in Russia aged 18 or over (no upper limit) from Indonesia, Russia, or ASEAN countries, with basic conversational English, a valid passport, and a Russian university student card.

faqs.question: Can ASEAN students join?
faqs.answer: Yes. Of the 35 places, 10 are reserved for students from ASEAN countries, alongside 15 Indonesian and 10 Russian participants.

faqs.question: What language is the camp in?
faqs.answer: The camp runs in Indonesian and Russian. Basic conversational English is required so everyone can interact across cultures.

faqs.question: What is the registration deadline?
faqs.answer: The exact deadline will be announced on this page and through PERMIRA St. Petersburg's channels (VK and Telegram).
